title: On the Antibacterial Action of Cultures of a Penicillium, with Special Reference to their Use in the Isolation of B. influenzae
version: Public-domain transcription of British Journal of Experimental Pathology 10:226–236, June 1929
lineage: Independent public-domain textual transcription of the original; image assets are not included. The article’s account concerns selective cultures, not systemic therapy.

passages.note: Table IV and surrounding paragraphs: Fleming and McLean tested paired culture plates from 25 influenza cases, using penicillin to suppress other organisms.
